title: ISTA-Net++: Flexible Deep Unfolding Network for Compressive Sensing

citations.claim: You et al. proposed ISTA-Net++, a flexible deep unfolding network that handles multiple compressive sensing ratios through a single trained model by incorporating a dynamic unfolding strategy.
ISTA-Net++ introduces a condition module that takes the CS ratio as input and transmits ratio-dependent step size and noise level parameters to each unfolded stage, enabling multi-ratio flexibility.
ISTA-Net++ uses a dynamic proximal mapping module (DPMM) consisting of residual blocks with convolution layers, replacing the hand-crafted proximal operator with a learned nonlinear mapping.
ISTA-Net++ introduces a cross-block strategy that processes the whole image rather than individual blocks, alleviating blocking artifacts and improving reconstruction quality by up to 0.64 dB PSNR.

ISTA-Net++ achieves state-of-the-art compressive sensing reconstruction with a single model containing 0.76M parameters, compared to prior methods that required separate models per CS ratio totaling up to 46.5M parameters.

You et al. demonstrated that using a balanced training dataset with diverse scenes improves robustness of deep unfolding networks, addressing the scene imbalance problem in the commonly used Train91 dataset.
ISTA-Net++ unfolds ISTA into K=20 stages, each alternating between a dynamic gradient descent module and a dynamic proximal mapping module corresponding to the gradient and proximal steps of ISTA.
The condition module in ISTA-Net++ uses three fully connected layers with ReLU and Softplus activations to predict per-stage step sizes and noise levels from the CS ratio input.

do_not_claim: ISTA-Net++ was the first to unfold ISTA for compressive sensing
ISTA-Net++ was applied to baseline correction or chromatography
ISTA-Net++ learns only scalar parameters per layer
